Load SCF Data as Multiply-Imputed Survey Design

Source: R/scf_load.R
scf_load.Rd

Loads .rds files created by scf_download() and converts them into multiply-imputed survey design objects. Each design object wraps 5 implicates using mitools::imputationList() and survey::svrepdesign(), enabling Rubin’s Rules–compliant analysis of SCF data with replicate weights.

scf_load(min_year, max_year = min_year, data_directory = ".")

Arguments

min_year

Earliest SCF year to load. Must be one of 1989, 1992, ..., 2022.

max_year

Latest SCF year to load. Defaults to min_year.

data_directory

Directory containing .rds files. Defaults to the current working directory.

Value

Invisibly returns a named list of successfully loaded years. Each SCF year is assigned into the global environment as a svrepdesign object (e.g., scf2019, scf2022), ready for use with the survey package.

Note

Files must have been generated using scf_download() and must contain all five implicates with correctly scaled replicate weights. Use scf_load() before running any scf_ analysis functions.

SCF Data Structure

Each SCF public release contains five implicates—independent versions of the dataset with imputed values for nonresponse items. This multiple imputation framework addresses item nonresponse, which is especially prevalent in household finance data due to privacy concerns, recall errors, and complexity of assets.

Instead of discarding incomplete cases or relying on a single imputation, the SCF follows best practices in multiple imputation to preserve sample size and reflect uncertainty from missing data. Final estimates are pooled across implicates using Rubin’s Rules.

For further details, see scf_MIcombine(), which wraps Rubin-style pooling for common estimation tasks.

Methodology

Each loaded .rds file contains five implicates created by scf_download(), each with 999 replicate weights (wt1b1 to wt1b999) scaled by their associated multiplicity adjustments. This function:

  • Reads each .rds file and verifies its structure

  • Wraps the five implicates in a mitools::imputationList()

  • Creates a custom survey replicate design using survey::svrepdesign(type = "other")

  • Sets design-level weights (wgt) and replicate weights

  • Stores the resulting object in the global environment

These designs enable valid point and variance estimation with full support for multiply-imputed data.

References

  • Federal Reserve Board. (2023). Survey of Consumer Finances. Public-Use Microdata Set. https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scfindex.htm

  • Kennickell, A.B. (2017). ""Multiple Imputation in the Survey of Consumer Finances" Statistical Journal of the IAOS Sage Publications.

See also

scf_download(), scf_MIcombine(), survey::svrepdesign(), mitools::imputationList()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load a single SCF year
scf_load(2022)

# Load a range of SCF years
scf_load(2010, 2022)

# Analyze a loaded object
scf_MIcombine(with(scf2022, svymean(~networth)))
} # }
